# Defy

> Defy is the insight and automation platform for agencies that punch above their weight: live competitor, audience and conversation intelligence (Defy Monitor), the ability to interrogate it inside Claude (Defy MCP), and agentic workflows that take the repetitive delivery off your team (Defy Agents) — the same capability the holding networks built for millions, without the build cost or maintenance burden.

Defy (Defy Group Limited) is the insight & automation platform for agencies that punch above their weight. Website: https://defygroup.ai/ · Platform login: https://cloud.defygroup.ai/ · Contact: talktous@defygroup.ai

## Platform
- Defy Monitor: live competitor, audience and conversation intelligence on every client and category.
- Defy MCP: interrogate that data inside Claude — prompt it like a co-worker, no dashboard to learn.
- Defy Agents: agentic workflows that handle repetitive delivery (e.g. reporting), so people focus on the work that wins.

## Who it is for
- Independent agencies (creative, media, CRM, influencer, PR, social) competing with holding-company networks.
- Brands with in-house teams wanting the networks' intelligence stack without agency margin.

## Clients
- SharkNinja (internal strategy team): Defy Monitor to understand LATAM markets and build test-and-learn strategies.
- SAMY (global influencer agency): Defy Agents cut performance reporting from three days to one.
- Enchant (UK CRM agency): Defy Monitor to automate CRM insight and campaign deployment.

## Founders
- Ian Cassidy — CEO & co-founder; 20 years in creative agencies; built and scaled SHARE Creative; private-equity exit to Bridgepoint.
- Alek Farseev — CTO & co-founder; AI professor based in Singapore; leads all technical development.

## Journal (English)
- [AI impact on agency jobs: how to rebuild the junior career ladder](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-entry-level-talent-ai/): AI is removing task-shaped agency work, not the need for people. Gartner found 18% of senior marketing leaders have cut some roles because of AI, while 16% have created new ones. Reporting, audits and resizing are most exposed. The best preparation is redesigning junior roles around judgement – questioning data, checking AI output and linking insight to outcomes – rather than halting graduate hiring.
- [Outcome-based agency remuneration: the metrics beyond ROAS and CPA](https://defygroup.ai/blog/beyond-roas-cpa-outcome-based-agency-pay/): Build outcome-based pay on metrics the client's finance team already trusts: incremental revenue measured by marketing mix modelling or holdout tests, contribution margin, new-customer growth and retention. Use ROAS and CPA as diagnostics, not fee triggers, because they are platform-reported and easy to game. Keep a fixed base fee, agree the measurement method upfront and add leading indicators the agency controls.
- [How to prove media ROI to clients: why MMM is back and what to show](https://defygroup.ai/blog/proving-media-roi-agencies-mmm/): Prove media ROI with layered evidence, not a ROAS screenshot. Use marketing mix modelling to show each channel's incremental contribution and saturation point, validate it with at least one holdout test, and explain why results moved using real audience and competitor evidence. Then present the findings as a reallocation of existing budget, which is easier for a client to approve than a request for more.
- [Marketing dashboard overload: why agencies are swapping logins for questions](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-dashboard-fatigue-ai-questions/): Start from the decision, not the data. List the handful of decisions you make for each client, write the one question each decision needs answered, and keep only the few metrics that answer it. Then use tools that let you ask that question in plain language and show the evidence behind the answer, instead of logging into another dashboard.
- [Brand differentiation strategy: finding the angle your category ignores](https://defygroup.ai/blog/escape-creative-sameness-category-intelligence/): Map what your whole category already says before deciding what you will say. Analyse competitors' ads and organic content for their messages, tones, visual codes and the audience tensions they address, then look for relevant tensions nobody owns. Choose the gap that is credible for your brand, brief creatives with the map rather than a template, and commit to it long enough to become familiar.
- [AI marketing tools for agencies: build a stack, not a shopping list](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-ai-stack-integration/): Choose AI marketing tools by how well they connect, not by their feature lists. Start from the two or three workflows that eat the most hours, map where the data has to flow, and pick tools that share one source of truth, show their working and can be written into client contracts. A connected stack of three beats a dozen clever apps that never talk.
- [Creative pre-testing: how to end the creativity vs performance war](https://defygroup.ai/blog/creativity-vs-performance-pre-testing/): Stop treating them as rivals and move the evidence earlier. Pre-test creative concepts before media spend, using scores as feedback to sharpen ideas rather than as verdicts after the money has gone. That lets bold, human work earn its place with evidence, keeps performance teams confident, and leaves the final call with people who understand the brand.
- [The agency sprint model: how to move fast without breaking strategy](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-sprint-model-speed-strategy/): Work in short, fixed sprints, but keep strategy outside the sprint. Decide the few things that must not change for a quarter, run tactics in sprints of days or weeks, and automate the monitoring, reporting and competitor checks that usually get skipped when time is tight. Speed comes from removing chores, not from removing rigour.
- [Synthetic audiences are taking off. Here's how agencies keep them honest](https://defygroup.ai/blog/synthetic-audiences-agencies-validation/): Synthetic audiences are reliable for speed, hypotheses and scenario testing, not as a substitute for real people. Treat every synthetic finding as a hypothesis, check it against observed behaviour such as what audiences actually publish and discuss, and validate the important ones with a small live test. If a conclusion can't be traced to real evidence, keep it out of the client deck.
- [Agentic AI advertising without the rogue fears: keep humans in the loop](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agentic-media-human-in-the-loop/): Let agents run the plumbing and keep people on meaning. Agents can plan, pace, optimise and report within limits you set, but humans should approve spend above agreed thresholds, own the message and tone, and plan from real audience conversations. Clear controls reassure clients; human judgement on what the brand says keeps customers' trust.
- [Audience research tools: what planners should automate first](https://defygroup.ai/blog/future-of-strategy-planners-automate/): Automate the gathering, not the thinking. Planners should hand audience research tools the high-frequency, low-judgement work first: competitor ad audits, social listening round-ups and first-draft personas built from real audience content. Insist that every AI conclusion links back to its source posts. Then reinvest the saved hours in what clients pay strategists for: judgement, sharper questions and the creative leap.
- [Influencer marketing reporting: why it's the new agency battleground](https://defygroup.ai/blog/influencer-agency-reporting-automation/): Measure influencer ROI by creator tier, with fully loaded costs that include agency hours, and benchmark cost per qualified engagement or conversion against paid social. Judge nano-influencers on trust signals such as saves, shares and purchase questions rather than likes. Automate data capture and comment classification, but keep the recommendations human and link every claim to the posts behind it.
- [Independent agency vs holding company: how independents compete on data](https://defygroup.ai/blog/independent-agencies-vs-holding-company-data/): Holding companies still lead on scale: proprietary platforms, media buying data and large specialist teams. But as network-grade analytics and AI become available on subscription, independents can match much of that capability without the build or maintenance cost. The deciding factor is shifting from who owns the data stack to who connects data to everyday client decisions fastest.
- [Agency consolidation or roster? What StarKist and ServiceNow reveal](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-consolidation-vs-roster/): Neither model wins by default. StarKist consolidated with one independent agency, Tombras, for fewer handovers and clearer accountability; ServiceNow chose a team of four Stagwell agencies tied to a technology partnership. In both cases the winning side showed it understood the client well enough to set expectations it could prove. Agencies win big accounts by making their promises measurable.
- [Will AI replace marketing agencies? Why the maths rarely adds up](https://defygroup.ai/blog/will-ai-replace-agencies/): Mostly not. AI replaces agency tasks such as campaign set-up, QA, report assembly and monitoring, but not accountability, relationships or judgement. Once you add the people, tools and management needed to run AI in-house, the saving often disappears. AI does threaten agencies that charge premium fees for admin. Used well, it frees agency teams for more creative, higher-value work.
- [Retail media networks and agencies: who really owns the budget?](https://defygroup.ai/blog/retail-media-agency-ownership/): Retail media should be owned strategically by whichever agency understands the client's category best, and executed by whoever has the strongest retailer access and tooling. The channel now spans retailer sites, social shops and creator content, so no agency type owns it by default. Independents win the strategy seat with continuous competitor and shopper intelligence, not buying scale.
- [How to reach Gen Z consumers: plan from communities, not birth years](https://defygroup.ai/blog/gen-z-persona-clustering/): Reach Gen Z by planning from real conversations, not age brackets. Cluster public posts, comments and reviews into personas defined by shared tensions, prove each one with real posts, then reach each cluster through the creators and formats it already chooses to watch. Measure saves, shares and substantive comments alongside reach, and refresh the clusters monthly.
- [AI video production cost: why cheaper frames don't shrink the budget](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-video-production-agency-economics/): AI makes each video asset cheaper, mainly in pre-production, versioning, resizing and localisation, but total budgets rarely fall because clients ask for more assets. Shoot costs such as crew, equipment and insurance are still rising in some markets. Agencies protect margin by automating repetitive work, keeping creative and cultural judgement human, and pricing the idea and the system rather than each frame.
- [How to optimise marketing budget ROI when global campaigns underdeliver](https://defygroup.ai/blog/global-vs-local-campaign-budget/): Start with creative fit, not media rates. Audit which assets run in each market, read local competitor and audience context, and score creative before buying media. Then move a ring-fenced share of low-confidence spend towards adapted or local work, with pre-agreed rules to scale or stop. Campaign reports new research finding that global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes.
- [Agency pitch strategy: win with a 48-hour category insight sprint](https://defygroup.ai/blog/win-agency-pitches-ai-category-insight/): Lead with the client's category, not your credentials. In the 48 hours after a brief lands, map competitors' paid and organic content, cluster the audience conversation into personas and tensions, and find the angle no competitor has claimed. Trace every claim to real ads and posts. An insight-led pitch gives the client a view it cannot compare on price.
- [AI-native marketing organisations: what clients still buy from agencies](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-native-marketing-organization-agencies/): An AI-native marketing organisation runs on its own data and AI layers, with a small team directing systems rather than doing tasks by hand. It needs fewer agency hours for reporting, optimisation and versioning, and more help building the system, centralising data, checking AI outputs, and supplying the creative and cultural judgement a model lacks.
- [AI marketing case studies with real numbers, and what they leave out](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-driven-agency-case-studies/): Credible AI marketing case studies are rarer than the hype suggests. The useful ones name a specific inefficiency, give a baseline, explain the method and say whether results are projected or realised. Recent examples include TRKKN's Meridian modelling for Faces, which projected an 8.5% revenue uplift, and SAMY cutting performance reporting from three days to one.
- [AI content creation best practices: a quality framework for agencies](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-content-quality-framework-agencies/): Treat AI output as raw material, not finished work. Write briefs that say where AI may be used and which decisions stay human, feed tools real audience evidence, edit for specificity rather than polish, pre-test concepts before media spend, record where AI shaped each asset, and judge results on business evidence instead of volume.
- [How AI hits each type of marketing agency: creative to influencer](https://defygroup.ai/blog/how-ai-disrupts-each-agency-type/): AI hits each agency type where its work is most repetitive and data-heavy: optimisation and reporting in media, production and versioning in creative, segmentation and deployment in CRM, monitoring in PR, and reporting in influencer. Because boutiques and networks now use the same tools, the advantage shifts to specialists who know things the tools do not.
- [Media consumption data in Singapore: what to trust as networks shrink](https://defygroup.ai/blog/apac-agencies-market-intelligence/): No single source gives you accurate media consumption data for Singapore. Use official statistics and regulator surveys for broad reach, audience measurement panels and platform data for exposure, and real published content for what people actually engage with and talk about. Compare them, note each one's blind spot, and treat precise averages with suspicion.
- [AI media planning: from demographics to real consumer tensions](https://defygroup.ai/blog/media-planning-real-personas-ai/): Use demographics as a filter, not a strategy. Age, gender or income tell you who to buy, but not why that person will pay attention. With AI you can cluster your audience’s real conversations into personas and tensions, then choose channels, messages and moments from those. Demographics come last, to narrow the buy.
- [Personalised advertising without losing trust: a guide for agencies](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ad-personalisation-without-third-party-data/): By personalising for context and culture before tracking. Niche audiences such as women’s football fans reward brands that show they understand their world: their heroes, their language and their gripes. You get there by listening to what they post, building variants for each group and testing which creative works before you spend. Trust is the precondition, not a side effect.
- [AI for independent agencies: why they’re consolidating and what changes](https://defygroup.ai/blog/independent-agency-consolidation-spain-ai/): The trend that matters isn’t a particular tool but a shift in scale. AI shortens execution and moves value towards research, strategy and coordinating specialisms, which is why independents are joining forces. But scale no longer requires headcount alone: an agency can tap into shared intelligence without merging, if it chooses its tools well.
- [AI data analysis in marketing: conclusions your clients can verify](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-data-analysis-verifiable-conclusions/): Treat every AI conclusion as a hypothesis until you can show the data behind it. Define the question before you open the tool, bring together sources that currently live in silos, insist on traceability back to the original data and review as a team before presenting. A conclusion nobody can verify is useless for decisions, however good it sounds.
- [Social listening for agencies: why the quarterly report is already too late](https://defygroup.ai/blog/continuous-social-listening-agencies/): With continuous social listening, not quarterly snapshots. The agency defines which categories, competitors and conversations it tracks for each client, reviews the signals every week against agreed action thresholds and checks every conclusion against the real posts behind it. That way it spots trends while they can still be used, not once competitors have claimed them.
- [Tariffs and marketing strategy: how to rebalance messages and budgets](https://defygroup.ai/blog/tariffs-marketing-strategy-messages-budgets/): Tariffs change the structure of your category: costs rise, consumers compare more and local substitutes appear. The answer isn’t to freeze investment but to map exposure by market, listen to how the price conversation is shifting, analyse which messages competitors are moving to and rebalance message and budget country by country, with short tests.
- [Agency burnout: fewer repetitive tasks, more time for creativity](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-burnout-automate-repetitive-work/): Managing agency stress starts with separating two loads: creative work, which is demanding but meaningful, and repetitive tasks such as reports, timesheets and format resizes. The second can be reduced or automated. Doing so frees up time and energy for the first and tackles one of the root causes of burnout. If the exhaustion persists, seek professional help.
- [Brand differentiation with AI: how not to sound like your competitors](https://defygroup.ai/blog/brand-differentiation-ai-without-sounding-generic/): Use AI to map what your whole category already says, not to write the message. Analyse competitors' ads and content, identify the crowded territories and the empty ones, develop an idea of your own in that gap and test the concepts before committing media spend. AI provides the map; human judgement provides the difference.
- [Agency pitches in Brazil: the new rules reward those who bring evidence](https://defygroup.ai/blog/brazil-agency-pitches-category-intelligence/): Turn up with evidence, not opinion. The updated Abracom and ABA guide calls for detailed briefs and transparent evaluation criteria, and warns that hiring an agency can't become an automated price comparison. That favours agencies that show, with real conversations and ads from the category, how consumers are changing and what the client's competitors are already doing.
- [Fragmented media consumption: understanding your audience beyond dashboards](https://defygroup.ai/blog/fragmented-media-consumption-audience-data/): Stop adding up platform reports and start with people. Gather what your audience posts, comments on and shares across every channel, cluster those conversations into personas and tensions, and only then allocate media. Fragmented data isn't fixed with more dashboards but with a common unit of analysis: the audience and what it actually says.
- [AI and the end of the holding company model: lessons for independent agencies](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-holding-company-model-independent-agencies/): Not overnight, but it's already changing it. Cuts at WPP and other groups show the junior-heavy pyramid giving way to lean, senior teams that orchestrate AI. For an independent agency, the advantage is having little structure and no legacy technology to pay for: you can adopt the same analytical capability without the cost of building it.
- [B2B content marketing that doesn't send decision-makers to sleep](https://defygroup.ai/blog/b2b-content-marketing-that-engages/): Swap what the brand wants to say for what the buyer feels they gain. B2B content engages when it starts from the real tensions of the people who decide (risk, timelines, budget, reputation), speaks their language and brings proof. Before investing in media, test several concepts and put money only behind those most likely to be clicked.
- [Black Friday for agencies: automate reporting, win back time to optimise](https://defygroup.ai/blog/black-friday-agencies-automate-reporting/): Decide early, automate the repetitive work and keep people free to make the calls during the peak. The Black Friday strategies that work depend on adjusting offer, creative and budget quickly, and that dies when the team spends the day building reports. Automate data collection, consolidation and alerts; keep people on budget, messaging and stock decisions with the client.
- [Engagement metrics clients value (and the ones that are window dressing)](https://defygroup.ai/blog/engagement-metrics-clients-value/): Separate attention metrics from business metrics, then connect one to the other. Likes and reach show that something happened; saves, shares, comments with intent, branded search and incremental revenue show that it mattered. Clients value the engagement you can connect to a decision: where to invest, what to cut, what to repeat.
- [Agency remuneration: how to prove your value with social data](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-remuneration-social-data-proof-of-value/): By turning social data into traceable proof. Buyers pay for time because it is the only thing they can verify. An agency that links each recommendation to the real posts of audiences and competitors, then to a metric agreed before the campaign, makes its value visible and can negotiate a hybrid or performance-based model.
- [Media agencies and AI: what the new era means for independents](https://defygroup.ai/blog/media-agencies-new-ai-era-independents/): AI absorbs execution first: reporting, data consolidation, repetitive optimisation. A media agency's value moves up towards advice, understanding the client's business and the ability to challenge a brief. For an independent, the point is not to pile up tools but to get the same depth of analysis as the big groups without bearing the cost of building it.
- [Research without respondents: are synthetic personas promise or mirage?](https://defygroup.ai/blog/respondent-free-research-synthetic-personas/): For exploring, yes; for concluding, no. Synthetic personas test scenarios and messages quickly, but they play back what the model has learned, generational clichés included, and claim no representativeness. For generational research, anchor every conclusion in real observed behaviour, such as the content these audiences actually publish, then use synthetic personas to test.
- [Imposter syndrome in agencies: rebuilding confidence in the AI era](https://defygroup.ai/blog/imposter-syndrome-agencies-ai-era/): Imposter syndrome thrives in agencies because work is judged constantly and rarely measured. AI makes it worse when you treat it as a rival, and eases it when it becomes a support. The most solid remedy: back your ideas with verifiable evidence, ask early and, for leaders, redesign junior roles rather than cut them.
- [Measuring cross-platform engagement: time to retire the agency spreadsheet](https://defygroup.ai/blog/measure-cross-platform-engagement-agencies/): No single tool does it alone, because every platform defines engagement differently. The reliable method: agree one shared definition of engagement, normalise metrics platform by platform, centralise the data in a single analysis layer and link the numbers to the conversations that explain them. Do that, and the hand-stitched spreadsheet becomes redundant.
- [Narrowing your agency's service offering: what to stop, and when](https://defygroup.ai/blog/when-to-stop-an-agency-service/): Stop a service when it is no longer differentiating, profitable or backed by the market you are targeting. The data usually tells you before the P&L does: clients bringing work in-house, cheaper competitors, formats declining in the category. According to Promethean Research, cited by Campaign US, agencies that narrowed their offer grew 13%, against 9.8% for those that expanded it.
- [Agency pricing models for AI: price it fairly, don't give away your margin](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-pricing-models-fair-ai-pricing/): Separate two things: the cost of the AI and the value of the output. Show licences and compute transparently, as a line item or a credit allowance, and price strategy, creative and media planning on outcomes rather than hours. Pass every efficiency gain on through lower fees and you make your work interchangeable – and therefore price-sensitive.
- [AI tools for agencies: how MCP gets you out of the tool sprawl](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-tools-agencies-mcp-integration/): Don't start with the tool; start with the workflows that eat the most time. Choose one central workspace, such as an AI assistant like Claude, and connect your data through open interfaces such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) rather than adding a new dashboard for every task. What matters is integration, traceability and clear sign-off rules.
- [Christmas 2026: social listening as an early-warning system for agencies](https://defygroup.ai/blog/christmas-2026-social-listening-early-warning/): Don't wait for sales data; watch what consumers are saying publicly and what competitors are running right now. Social listening shows early whether price pressure, gift uncertainty or delivery worries are growing. Set a baseline in October, agree thresholds with the client and get alternative messages signed off before Black Friday on 27 November.
- [The cold-start problem: how to personalise ads when you have no user data](https://defygroup.ai/blog/cold-start-ad-personalisation-public-personas/): To begin with, personalise at the level of personas, not people. Analyse your category's public conversations, comments, reviews and creator content, distil them into personas with clear motives and tensions, and match new users using early signals such as landing page, search term or context. With every interaction, your own first-party data replaces the starting assumptions.
- [AI and consumer behaviour: why agencies need to rebuild their insight work](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-consumer-behaviour-rebuild-agency-insights/): AI is shifting how people search, discover and trust: questions to assistants supplement the search engine, algorithms curate feeds, and interchangeable content loses credibility. Agencies should therefore gather insight more often and closer to real behaviour – from public conversations and content rather than annual surveys alone – and check every AI conclusion against the evidence behind it.
- [AI adoption in agencies: document the real workflow before you automate](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-bad-process-document-workflows-first/): Start with the work, not the tool. Sit with the people who actually do the job, map how it really moves rather than what the SOP says, and find the single bottleneck: the brief, production, approval, the handover or a decision. If you can't name it, don't automate anything yet. AI applied to a broken process just gives you a faster broken process.
- [AI-native agency: why speed isn't progress, and the 5 levels that are](https://defygroup.ai/blog/speed-is-not-progress-ai-native-agencies/): An AI-native agency is one where AI is built into how work flows, so frontline experts benefit without having to open a chatbot. You get there in levels, from chat-based prompting to agents sharing one source of truth. Most agencies don't need level five. Define the finish line, the time and the resources, then stop at the level that removes your bottleneck.
- [AI roles in agencies: stop making AI everyone's job](https://defygroup.ai/blog/stop-making-ai-everyones-job-builders-users-approvers/): No. Everyone benefits from AI; not everyone needs to build it. Agencies that handed every employee a code account found half the team thrived and half didn't, leaving a mess of unmaintained tools. A better model uses three roles: builders who invest extra time, users who run the systems daily and report problems, and approvers who sign off quality before anything ships.
- [Closed-loop AI for agencies: from eleven tools to one shared layer](https://defygroup.ai/blog/one-shared-layer-agency-ai-closed-loop/): Stop adding tools and build one shared layer they all read from: memory (one source everything reads), skills (repeatable jobs encoded), workflow (how work really moves) and approvals (a person signs before anything ships). Then close the loop by logging every call, email and decision where AI can see it. Gaps in what you capture become gaps in what AI knows.
- [How to measure AI ROI in an agency: define success before you deploy](https://defygroup.ai/blog/define-success-before-deploying-ai-agency/): Decide what success looks like before you switch anything on. Measure how the work performs today (baseline), set the improvement that would justify the change (target), run the AI workflow against the old way (test), then count the full cost, including checking and fixing output (review). If editing AI output eats the time it saved, you haven't gained anything.
- [AI metrics for agencies: why clients pay for results, not usage](https://defygroup.ai/blog/measure-ai-results-not-usage-agencies/): Track outcomes, not usage. AI users, tasks automated, agents deployed and assets generated are vanity metrics. The AI metrics clients value are cost per output, time to output, quality or error rate, and profit impact. Add an acceptance rate for AI output and feed every correction back into the system, so 'good enough' becomes genuinely good and the numbers can support outcome-based fees.
- [Agency AI strategy: don't build what Meta and Google will automate](https://defygroup.ai/blog/dont-build-what-platforms-automate-agencies/): Don't spend your AI budget rebuilding what Meta and Google are automating: audience targeting, ad creation, keyword lists and campaign setup. Use the platforms' native tools, buy rather than build everything else because someone has to maintain it, and focus your people on the work where expertise and client judgement are the product: insight, strategy, creative and advice.
- [AI resistance in agencies is a standards problem, not a people problem](https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-resistance-standards-not-people/): AI resistance in agencies usually signals a quality problem, not a people problem. Experienced staff resist when AI output falls below their standards and they are forced to redo it. Fix it by letting subject-matter experts define what good looks like and approve AI work, measuring editing time rather than log-ins, and starting with low-risk chores where the time saved is real.
- [AI readiness assessment for agencies: why your weakest dimension decides](https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-ai-readiness-four-dimensions/): An AI readiness assessment for agencies should score four dimensions: context (what is written down for AI to use), people (who gets real work from AI), process (how work really runs) and platform (what you pay for and how deeply it is used). Your weakest dimension sets your readiness, so fix that first. AI courses alone rarely move it.
- [What to automate in an agency: three questions to answer first](https://defygroup.ai/blog/before-you-automate-three-questions-agencies/): Before automating anything in an agency, answer three questions: how complex is the decision, how much damage could a bad output cause, and what measurable outcome would improve? Start with high-reward, low-risk tasks that need moderate expertise, such as reporting, resizing and monitoring. Leave high-risk, high-expertise work, like budget calls and client strategy, to people.
